english.legislation: Contrary to section 21(1) and (2) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006.

english.notes:
Section 21(3) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 provides that this offence shall be treated as:-
(a) a relevant offence for the purpose of sections 28B and 28D of the Immigration Act 1971 (search, entry and arrest), and (b) an offence under Part III of that Act (criminal proceedings) for the purposes of sections 28E, 28G and 28H (search after arrest).Important Note - The wording of section 21(1) and the sentence available was amended on 12th July 2016 by section 35 of the Immigration Act 2016. For any offence committed before this date, H9302 (CJS code IA06001) should be used.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.Time limit on prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
